content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe and explain experiments to investigate photosynthesis
Test a leaf for starch to show photosynthesis has occurred

Classic experiments on photosynthesis have helped scientists understand the process. These experiments investigate what is needed for photosynthesis and can measure its rate. Testing for starch in leaves is a common way to show photosynthesis has occurred.
Glucose converts to starch for storage
Iodine test is simple and reliable
- Place in boiling water for 30 seconds
- Place in boiling ethanol (in water bath)
Ensures starch found is from experiment
Show that light is needed for photosynthesis
Cover part of leaf with foil (light-proof)
Show that chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis
Use a variegated leaf (green and white parts)

content.text: Set up pondweed in water bath
Measure oxygen production at each temperature
Rate increases with temperature (up to a point)
Use water bath, no naked flames
Eye protection, keep away from heat
The starch test directly tests for photosynthesis
It tests for starch, which indicates glucose production from photosynthesis
Any light source works equally well
Different light intensities give different results
They're mostly oxygen but may contain other gases
Boiling the leaf in ethanol removes chlorophyll directly
The ethanol must be hot (via water bath) to dissolve chlorophyll
Remove starch from plant by keeping in dark
Leaf with green and white areas
Aquatic plant used to measure photosynthesis
Provides CO₂ for aquatic plant experiments
Starch test: kill leaf → remove chlorophyll → soften → iodine
Destarch plants before experiments (24-48 hours dark)
Light requirement: cover part of leaf, test for starch
CO₂ requirement: use soda lime to remove CO₂
Rate measured by counting bubbles or collecting gas from pondweed
Variables: light intensity, CO₂ concentration, temperature
Safety: water bath for ethanol, eye protection
